summary.one_liner: A musical instrument strobe tuner that measures pitch from microphone input and shows cents deviation, frequency, and a strobe display.
summary.what_it_does: Listens to an instrument through the microphone and displays the detected note, deviation in cents, correct and actual frequency, and reference pitch. It shows an oscilloscope view of the input waveform and a spectrum display that can be zoomed to about ±50 cents around the current note. A strobe display shifts left or right to indicate flat or sharp, and a meter shows the deviation in cents. The Options window adds a filter for low notes, a downsampling mode, a display lock, multiple-value display, reference adjustment, and a clock correction factor for inaccurate audio hardware. The README says it uses an overlapped FFT with phase-difference analysis to measure frequency, and it can also be tuned to accordions or melodeons.
use_cases: tune a guitar or other instrument by ear with a visual display
check the pitch of low notes with a harmonic-reducing filter
copy tuning readings to another application
calibrate a tuner against a known reference frequency
how_to_run: Play your instrument into your microphone and observe the display.
stack: Windows and Mac versions named in the README
Android version named in the README, also on F-Droid
notable: Strobe display with cents and frequency readout
Clock correction factor for inaccurate sound cards
caveats: README does not state installation steps or platform requirements beyond the listed Windows, Mac and Android versions
Downsampling mode generates spurious subharmonics that must be ignored
Correction value is only saved after clicking the save button
